purpose: Ublituximab-Xiiy is used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS) in adults. This includes people who have had relapses or flare-ups of MS symptoms over time. It helps reduce the number of relapses and slows the progression of disability.
how_it_works: Your immune system has certain white blood cells called B-cells, and in MS, these cells mistakenly attack your nervous system. This medication works by targeting and reducing the number of those harmful B-cells in your body. By lowering the number of these B-cells, the drug helps calm down the immune system's attack on your nerves, which can reduce MS flare-ups.
common_side_effects: Infusion reactions such as fever, chills, headache, flushing, or nausea during or shortly after the IV infusion. You may also experience more frequent infections such as upper respiratory infections or urinary tract infections. Feeling tired or having a headache is also common.
warnings: This medication can increase your risk of serious infections, including a rare but dangerous brain infection called PML. You should not receive live vaccines while on this medication. Tell your doctor right away if you develop signs of infection such as fever, chills, or confusion. Women who are pregnant or planning to become pregnant should talk to their doctor, as this drug may harm a developing baby. Hepatitis B can reactivate in people who have had it before, so you will be tested prior to starting treatment.
typical_dosing: This medication is given through an IV (intravenous infusion) in a clinic or infusion center. The first dose is given as two separate infusions — one on Day 1 and another one two weeks later. After that, it is given as a single infusion every 6 months. Each infusion takes about one hour, but you will be monitored before and after for a period of time.
